11                 GURU DILEEPJI:   Honorable 

12    President, Senators, and public servants, 

13    Namaste.  The divine within me bows to the same 

14    divine within you.  

15                 It is a great honor and privilege to 

16    offer an invocation at this esteemed Senate of 

17    the New York State Legislature.  I extend my 

18    gratitude to the Honorable President of the 

19    Senate for permitting me to chant ancient 

20    Vedic prayers.  

21                 I also wish to express my sincere 

22    thanks to Senator Honorable Jessica Spanton for 

23    her kind invitation to deliver this invocation 

24    today.  

25                 I will begin with blowing the conch 


                                                                5448

 1    shell, followed by Vedic prayers in Sanskrit and 

 2    their contents' English translation.  

 3                 (Blowing conch shell.)

 4                 (Chanting prayers.)

 5                 GURU DILEEPJI:   Om!  I connect with 

 6    the Earth's energy and the divine light of the 

 7    Sun.  May this light awaken our spiritual 

 8    awareness.

 9                 We thank Tryambaka for prosperity.  

10    Like a cucumber grows away from its stem, I claim 

11    my freedom from death.

12                 May everyone have well-being, peace, 

13    and good fortune.

14                 May all be happy, healthy, and may 

15    no one suffer.

16                 Lead me from untruth to truth, from 

17    darkness to light, and from death to immortality.

18                 The infinite universe comes from the 

19    infinite.

20                 Om!  May everyone be happy.

21                 In closing, O Lord of the Universe, 

22    guide our New York State Senators and honorable 

23    public servants.  Grant them wisdom and 

24    compassion of all New Yorkers.  

25                 Help us remember that we all deserve 


                                                                5449

 1    respect and dignity regardless of our 

 2    backgrounds.  May we listen and learn from one 

 3    another to promote understanding and 

 4    collaborations.

 5                 Begin the day with love, spend the 

 6    day with love, fill the day with love, and end 

 7    the day with love.  This is the way how we 

 8    connect with the divine essence of the universe.

 9                 May we always be blessed by the 

10    divine.  In unison we affirm:  Love all, serve 

11    all.

12                 Thank you, and Namaste.

 5                 THE SECRETARY:   Resolution 2106, by 

 6    Senator Brisport, recognizing Second Chance Month 

 7    in the State of New York and recognizing the 

 8    profound mental health impacts of incarceration 

 9    on individuals, families, and communities.

10                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Senator 

11    Brisport on the resolution.

12                 SENATOR BRISPORT:   Thank you, 

13    Mr. President.

14                 I rise today to introduce a 

15    resolution formally recognizing the month of 

16    April as Second Chance Month in the State of 

17    New York.  

18                 Second Chance Month brings critical 

19    awareness to the immense mental health barriers 

20    formerly incarcerated individuals face during 

21    reentry.  

22                 Incarceration inflicts severe, 

23    lasting psychological trauma.  Prolonged 

24    isolation, violence and family separation do not 

25    rehabilitate, they tear at the mental stability 


                                                                5454

 1    of individuals and create ripples of trauma that 

 2    impact families and entire communities.  When 

 3    people return home, they face systemic gaps in 

 4    care and deep-seated stigma.  

 5                 If we truly want to reduce 

 6    recidivism and advance public health, New York 

 7    State must take responsibility for these mental 

 8    health consequences.  

 9                 Of course, we cannot address this 

10    systemic trauma without honoring those who turn 

11    their lived experience into a lifeline for 

12    others.  Joining us in the gallery today is an 

13    extraordinary leader, Shawanna Vaughn.  

14                 Shawanna's life is a testament to 

15    reliance.  Born in a California prison hospital 

16    to an incarcerated mother, she experienced the 

17    foster-care system and youth incarceration.  She 

18    survived cancer, and she suffered the devastating 

19    loss of her brother to gang violence.  Yet she 

20    refused to let systemic trauma have the final 

21    word.  

22                 Instead, she chose a path of radical 

23    transformation.  Perhaps one of the most powerful 

24    chapters of Shawanna's story is that she was able 

25    to forgive her brother's murderer.  As she has 


                                                                5455

 1    beautifully said, "Redemption is for everyone.  

 2    It was important for me to forgive so that I 

 3    could continue my own healing."  

 4                 That is true.  That is the true 

 5    beating heart of what a second chance means.  A 

 6    second chance is not just an administrative box 

 7    to check; it is the profound human capacity for 

 8    redemption and healing.  

 9                 Shawanna took that philosophy and 

10    founded Silent Cry, Inc., a New York-based 

11    nonprofit dedicated to taking a holistic approach 

12    to aftercare from mass incarceration, gun  

13    violence and trauma.  

14                 Silent Cry provides essential grief 

15    counseling, trauma-informed resources, and 

16    support for families navigating the aftermath of 

17    the justice system.  

18                 By adopting this resolution today, 

19    this legislative body pauses to recognize the 

20    deep mental health trauma associated with 

21    incarceration.  We call for the awareness and 

22    research necessary to address these harms so 

23    New York can truly embody the spirit of a second 

24    chance.  

25                 Thank you, Mr. President.  I extend 


                                                                5456

 1    my deepest gratitude to Shawanna Vaughn and 

 2    Silent Cry for their life-saving advocacy, and I 

 3    yield the floor.
